notes.title: Minor Bug Fixes to player movement
notes.content:
Minor Bug Fixes to player movement and Maze Generation: 

 Player character no longer jitters while pressing and holding the mouse over it.
 Player character no longer tries to move while settings is open.
 Maze Generation better adjusts to fit larger-sized answers on rugs.

notes.title: Magic Math Maze
notes.content:
Introducing a new way to play: Mazes! 
Step into the Magic Math Maze and find your way to the solution to dispel the magical maze and earn stars. Finding your way out of the maze earns Maze and Random achievement progress in addition to the type of problem that was solved. 


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44987311/9abda4406b926c596c3af76385d1790e6a57431a.gif"]

Other Updates or minor fixes:  

Clocks- The Hour hand now moves more accurately. For example, at 4:30, instead of pointing directly at 4, it points between 4 and 5.

notes.title: March 2025 - The Counting Time Update
notes.content:
The Counting Time Update introduces two new math modes to Runi's Math Castle 


Counting
For beginners just learning their numbers, introducing the "Count" room. Your child will be presented with a set of objects for them to count them select the correct number. The objects are colored to match their character. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44987311/4901e2405548049664493a1ff604be0d0cc05ce3.gif

Analog Clock 
For kids farther along in their number journey, introducing the Clock room. Upon entering the room, an analog clock’s hours and minutes hands rotate into position for them to practice reading the time. The clock starts with only the hour numbers showing and when a hint is requested, the minutes appear. Color codes help strengthen the association between shorthand to hours and long hand to minutes. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44987311/54f45dd241d9a3053544a186d34eb8c981960cd4.gif

Other update and fixes: 


 Settings number selectors updated to work easier and in more expected ways. 
 Settings updated to enable or disable all game modes, not just the advanced ones. 
 Multiplication is now able to show a hint of crossing lines. 
 Resolved a bug causing the wrong scoreboard to open in the math room when checking the math high scores. 
 Resolved a bug with the Back Arrow sometimes showing in the wrong location.

notes.title: Update Notes for Nov 28, 2024
notes.content:
Hi Ya'll, 
Here are the changes for this release of Runi's Math Castle:

Cleaned up the image for the playing card suites. 

A countdown timer was added to signal the start of the Dance Party and Spire Jump mini-games. This is to make the transition into playing these timed games less jarring. 

Settings configuration saving methodology has been updated, causing Settings configuration to revert to default. Scoreboard tracking and Game/Character unlocks are unaffected. These changes allow me to include other math modes in the future without breaking old configuration settings again. 

Ejnoy!

notes.title: Design Talk
notes.content:
Hey Ya'll, 

I wanted to take some time to talk about some of the design decisions that were important to in making this project. I’m not a formally educated educator, nor do I have any formal training in child or gaming psychology, but I have been following the news, and I am a mother myself, so I have made some very conscious choices in how the reward system plays out in Runi’s Math Castle. 

Unlockables - First is the choice to have bonus content (skins and mini-games) be purchasable instead of randomly rewarded. Given the connection between loot-boxes and gambling addictions, I decided against any kind of random reward system. Also, letting the player choose what to unlock with the rewards increases agency. 

Math Questions - Every math question is structured with 5 possible answers. The starting reward value is 3 stars. Each wrong guess reduces the number of stars the correct answer is worth. Three wrong guesses and the correct answer is revealed, awarding no stars. I’ve seen my kid play games that let her keep answering until she gets it right, and that leads to her “button mashing” until she’s rewarded, which is not the thoughtful experience I wanted to create here.

Reveal Reward - The kid play testers figured out quickly that answering the question correctly the first time got them more stars, which encouraged them to solve the problem correctly. The stars are hidden until earned so that wrong answers don’t cause a star to go away and unnecessarily dissuade the player.

Number Range - The original goal was to let older kids turn up the difficulty by growing the number range past the initial 0 - 10 and including negatives when they are ready. What I wasn’t expecting was for younger kids to turn the number range up very high and just go crazy seeing the very large numbers in the math problems. Happy side effects.

Encouraging Daily Practice - Rather than work in some fomo gimmick for a daily login bonus, I incorporated score boards. Scores for Math problems and mini-games get tracked each day encouraging players to try and beat their best whenever they can come play.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44987311/518a39de5e0ee9807b1c933991bf941a8f0cc842.gif

- caio 
Nicole

notes.title: Steam Page For Runi's Math Castle is launched.
notes.content:
Hello everyone, 
    Today is such an exciting day for me, being able to launch the Steam page for Runi's Math Castle. This has been a passion project for me for the past several months squeezed in between working full time, going to online collage, being a wife and mother... but with a little passion and a lot of dedication, here I am. 

    There are still a few items that need to be finished before the full game launch in the summer of 2024:
- The main technical challenge remaining is testing controller support. Ideally I've already made everything controller compatible, but only testing will tell for certain. 
- Art wise, I still have some animation for some of the characters to finish and polish up. 
- Music and sound effects are in development. 

I hope everyone has a much fun running around the Castle as I had bringing it to life. 

Ciao
